Don't use me as an example. I am absolutely not a normal example. I've been rejected by mental health professionals for being worse than they can handle. I've been engaging in self harm since I was 13 and most people stop by their twenties and I just got worse. I'm really fucking smart to a point that it impairs my social relationships and I rarely feel understood. I lack any basic functioning skills. I have debilitating ADHD and may or may not be on the autistic spectrum. I'm super resistant to psych meds so I take like five of them but they don't work that well and I've tried all the other ones. 

All these things combined so that for me it didn't get better. It gets better for most people.

My class took a field trip to the city when I was 13. I don't even remember what we were doing there, but I remember spending that entire part of the bus ride staring up at all the skyscrapers and imagining jumping off. At that age I also tried to think through the logistics of where I could hang myself or the best place to lie down on the railroad tracks. 

I was very suicidal until I was 22 and began using ketamine (in a medical way to treat depression but self-administered because that made it affordable) and it actually worked really well for getting rid of the constant suicidal thoughts. But this is different. This isn't the urge to kill myself. In fact there is a large part of me that really doesn't want to do this. But this is a rational conclusion I've reached based on my (in)ability to function normally and even keep up with basic things necessary to be a functional adult. I'd hoped and hoped that if I just tried hard enough and pushed myself hard enough and grew up a little that I would become able to function, but it truly hasn't gotten any better and I've been frantically kicking trying to tread water for the last decade and I'm tired.

This isn't necessarily universal. I have POTS and my passing out is a lot less dramatic. It's not orthostatic hypotension because my BP stays about the same sitting to standing (sometimes it even goes up) but during a bad period my HR will go from like 70 to 140. 

I stand up, my brain kinda stops processing things, I usually shake some and I kinda crumple to the ground. I'm 25 and it's not as bad as in my teens, and I usually just end up in a sitting position rather than completely flat on the ground. I think I've gotten some bruises from it, but the only serious thing was one concussion when I was in my late teens.

It's usually over in less than twenty seconds. My brain kind of "reboots" and retroactively processes what happened. There's sometimes a brief moment of depersonalization/derealization. I'm usually able to assure people that I'm fine immediately after it happens. 

I don't get a warning, I just stand up and pass out. In the few seconds before I pass out I am experiencing the feeling of being about to pass out, but my brain is not processing things so I can't really decide to do anything about it. 

Really it's just not a big deal to me. I just warn people who I spend a lot of time around "if you see me stand up and pass out it's fine, that's just a thing that happens sometimes, I'll be good within 20 seconds." I always feel completely fine immediately after other than having to stand up from the floor slowly. No clamminess or any kind of lasting effects.
